article_content: A dilapidated house in Sydney's south-east has sold for $2.17 million at auction, exceeding its $1.6 million reserve price. Located at 268 Doncaster Ave, Kensington, the property was sold to an investor. Estate agent Joe Recep of NG Farah Real Estate described the house as 'very run down'. Despite its condition, it attracted 27 registered bidders. The house had been in the same family for 50 years and was used as a rental property for eight years, primarily to university students due to its proximity to the University of New South Wales.

Bakka 268 Doncaster Ave, Kensington jedhamutti argamu kan ta'e mana kana namni qarshii itti dabalate gurgurateera. Hoggansi manneen gurguratanii Jo Recep NG Farah Real Estate 'baayyee gad bu'aa ture' jedheera. Yeroo gurguramu namoonni 27 galuun isaanii beeksisanii turan. Mana kana maatii tokkoon waggaa 50 oliif kan turaniidha, waggaa saddeetf ammoo kan namoota biraa akka jiraatan godhanii turan, akkasumas kan Yunivaarsitii New South Wales itti dhihoo waan ta'eef barattoonni yunivaarsitii akka jiraatan godhan.

article_content: Passengers on a United Airlines flight from San Francisco to Sydney that was diverted to Canberra were stuck on board for over 19 hours and on the tarmac for another four. The flight, UA 863, was diverted due to debris on Sydney's runway and landed in Canberra at 9am on Friday. Since Canberra is not an international airport, it lacks customs, quarantine, and immigration facilities, so passengers couldn't disembark. Some passengers began their journey in New York and reported being on a plane for 30 hours. A passenger told Daily Mail Australia they were kept on the plane without food, water, or access to bathrooms for three hours until Qantas provided snacks. Officials allowed passengers to disembark just after 1pm but they had to stay on the tarmac under the guard of Australian Federal Police officers and customs officials. A replacement pilot crew arrived in Canberra around 3:30pm, and the plane took off for Sydney at 5pm.

Geetii UA 863 jedhamu kun gara 'Sydney' imalu kan hafee 'Canberra' qubatee jira sababiin isaas 'Sydney' karaa geetiin itti qubatu irratti wanti bidiruu keessa jiru argameef. Sababiin isaas 'Canberra' 'airport' idil-addunyaa miti, kanneen akka 'customs', 'quarantine', fi 'immigration facilities' hin qabu, kanaafis namoonni geetaa irraa bu'uu hin dandeenye. Namoonni tokko tokko imala isaanii 'New York' jalqabanii hanga ammaatti 30 sa'atii geetaa keessa akka turan himan. Nama tokko 'Daily Mail Australia' gabaase akka jedhetti, namoonni geetaa keessa sa'atii sadiif marfamanii turan, wanti akka 'nyaataa fi bishaanii fi manneen kuusuu hin qabanneef. Sana booda 'Qantas' nyaata xiqqaa namootaaf kenneef. Hoggantootni namoota gara 'tarmac' akka ba'an hayyamaniiru garuu jala 'Australian Federal Police officers' fi 'customs officials' jalatti turan. Gareen 'pilootii' bakka bu'uu dhufe 'Canberra' sa'atii 3:30 fi gareen imala gara 'Sydney' imaluu itti fufe sa'atii 5:00.

article_content: Canada is set to conclude its combat mission in Afghanistan by July and will assume a new role in the war-torn nation, focusing on security, diplomacy, human rights, and development. Foreign Minister Lawrence Cannon stated that 'Canada is committed to helping build a more secure, stable, and self-sufficient Afghanistan that is no longer a safe haven for terrorists.' The Canadian government estimates the cost of this new role to be around '$700 million (US $694.5 million) a year from 2011 to 2014.', with the final costs to be determined after 2014. Canada will continue to train Afghan security forces and provide humanitarian aid, with a particular focus on improving the lives of Afghan women and supporting the G-8 Initiative on Maternal, Newborn and Child Health.

Ministeerri Alaa Lawrence Cannon 'Kanadaa Afganistaan nageenya qabu, tasgabbaa'e fi of danda'uu ta'e ijaaruuf gumaacha godhuuf waadaa galteera' jedhe. Mootummaan Kanadaa baaja tilmaama '$700 miliyoona (US $694.5 miliyoona) waggaa tokkoof bara 2011 hanga 2014tti' ta'uu himera, baajiin dhumaatiis erga bara 2014 booda beekama. Kanadaa leenjii humni nageenyaa Afganistaan ni itti fufsiisa, deeggarsa namoomaa kan akka gargaarsa G-8 Initiative on Maternal, Newborn and Child Health ni kenniti.

Harman worked four days a week at the University of Nebraska Medical Center well into his 90s, despite retiring in 1986.

Dr. Harman bara 1986 hojii irraa deemee osoo jiruu, waggaa 90'ntti guyyaa afur tokkoon Centre Medical University of Nebraska keessatti hojjachuu itti isaa turan.

article_content: Steven Gerrard became the third player in Liverpool's history to make 700 appearances during their FA Cup fourth-round replay against Bolton. Recalled by Brendan Rodgers, Gerrard joined Ian Callaghan and Jamie Carragher in Liverpool's 700 club. Gerrard wore special boots with 'No 700' and his daughters' names, 'Lilly' and 'Lexie', to mark the occasion. Having spent his entire career at Liverpool, Gerrard is set to leave for LA Galaxy in the summer. Liverpool won against Bolton with late goals from Raheem Sterling and Philippe Coutinho, advancing to the fifth round.

The University of Minnesota tops the list, followed by Arizona State University and SUNY Buffalo. This conclusion was reached after polling over 10,000 members about their educational backgrounds. The University of Minnesota had the highest number of members on the site. article_content: 'Oil from the spill could turn Gulf marshlands into open water, affecting millions of migratory birds for generations,' said Tom Moorman, senior science official at Ducks Unlimited. 'It took over 50 years for the plant root network at the Mississippi River base to form,' he added. Louisiana's marshland shrunk by 60% since the turn of the century, from 3 million to 1.2 million acres. Over 13 million migratory birds visit the Gulf marshlands each winter. 'If oil lingers in the marshlands through late summer and fall, it will affect millions of birds,' Moorman said. Ryan Lambert, a fishing tour captain, reported significant business cancellations. Moorman stressed that prevention is crucial as oil removal from wetlands is challenging.

'Waggaa 50 oliif lafa baalaafi qilleensa Mississippi River keessa jiru kan miidhamaa ture yoo ta'u, ammallee itti fufee jira,' jedhe. Lafa baalaafi qilleensa Louisiana keessa jiru miliyoona 3 irraa gara miliyoona 1.2tti hir'ate. 'Yoo bishaan gubachaa hanga dhuma haagaafi xiqqoo keessa lafa baalaafi qilleensa keessatti hafe, lakkoofsa baayyee kanneen magariisaa miidhaa ni geessisa,' jedhe Moorman. Ryan Lambert, hooggana daawwii daandeffamaafi qilleensa irratti bobba'an, himate dhabamsiisuu danda'a.

article_content: The leader of a criminal gang suspected of conspiring with Mexican police to kill 43 missing students in Guerrero has been detained. The students went missing near Iguala on September 26 after clashing with police and masked men. Authorities have arrested dozens of police linked to 'Guerreros Unidos,' a gang that split from the Beltran Leyva Cartel. The Attorney General's office is holding 27 municipal policemen involved in the attack. Over 1,200 security forces are searching for the students. The gang's leader, Sidronio Casarrubias Salgado, was captured along with a collaborator, weapons, and vehicles. Attorney General Jesus Murillo Karam said the arrest marked 'the beginning of a new route of investigation.' Thousands protested in Acapulco demanding the students' safe return.

Barattoonni kun kan badani yeroo polisiin fi namoonni maaskotaa qabatanii wajjin walitti bu'anii turan. Poolisiin hedduun kan qabaman 'Guerreros Unidos' jedhamuutti kan walqabatan yoo ta'u, gareen kunis kan baqate 'Beltran Leyva Cartel' jedhamu irraa. Ministira Muummee Yakkattoo Dr. Jesus Murillo Karam akka jedhanitti qabamni kun 'kaawwayyuun qorannoo haaraa kan nutti fida' jedhan.

article_content: Research indicates that middle-aged women who regularly engage in vigorous physical activities like aerobics, Zumba, or spinning classes have a lower risk of developing breast cancer. A study following 126,000 post-menopausal women over three years found that those doing three hours of vigorous exercise weekly had a 21% lower risk of breast cancer compared to those who did little or no exercise. The research, conducted by Oxford University, also highlighted that women with higher body fat were 55% more likely to develop breast cancer than slimmer women. Experts suggest that while being overweight is known to increase breast cancer risk due to higher oestrogen levels from fat cells, vigorous exercise may offer additional protective benefits beyond just weight management.

Qorannoo dubartoota 126,000 kan waggaa sadiif hordofameen, warri torbanitti sa'aatii sadiif sochii cimaa gochan carraa kanserii gara 21% gadi bu'uu argame. Qorannoo Yuunivarsiitii Oxford kan geggeeffameen, dubartoota baayyee mishiin qaban carraa kanserii 55% ol ta'uu argame. Oggoonni sochii cimaan faayidaa qabu kan argamu akkaataa ulfaatina qaamaa qofarratti osoo hin taane mala biraatiin ta'uu ni mala.

article_content: The London Crossrail project is set to excavate the remains of historical figures, including a former lord mayor of London, notorious criminals, and political activists, from an infamous burial ground. Research led by Crossrail has identified the names and backgrounds of over 5,000 individuals buried at the old Bedlam cemetery site beneath Liverpool Street in London. Among those identified are Sir Ambrose Nicholas, who served as lord mayor of London in 1575, and Dr John Lamb, an astrologer and advisor to the First Duke of Buckingham. The excavation will unearth around 3,000 skeletons from the site, which includes remains of former patients from Bethlem Royal Hospital, known as Bedlam. The hospital is considered the world's first mental asylum, having treated patients as early as the 14th century. The Bedlam burial ground was established in 1569 to cope with overcrowding during plague outbreaks. The archaeological work is being conducted by the Museum of London Archaeology on behalf of Crossrail. Scientific analysis of the skeletons will provide insights into the lives and deaths of early modern Londoners.

Qorannoon Crossrail duraanii geggeessaa tureen maqaa fi haala 5,000 ol ta'an kanneen bakka itti awwaalan Bedlam jedhamu jala Liverpool Street London 'itti argamu irratti beekameera. article_content: 'The high upfront cost of electric vehicles remains a significant barrier for many consumers looking to switch from gas-powered cars,' and there are additional 'hidden costs' that are not immediately obvious. A Scottish Tesla owner recently received a '£17,374 ($21,000) repair bill' after his vehicle's battery was damaged by rain, illustrating the potential financial risk. 'Although government tax credits can offset the initial purchase price,' EVs are still more expensive than their gas-powered counterparts, largely due to the high cost of production. According to a survey by Recurrent, '1.5% of 15,000 EV owners required battery replacements' at a cost of between '$5,000 and $20,000.' article_content: In the midst of heated political campaigns and real wars abroad, two columnists writing for 'The New York Times' took a different tack on Sunday, ending up in the same place: a discussion on sexual nihilism and the modern woman. Maureen Dowd's column, 'She's Fit to Be Tied,' looks at E.L James's 'Fifty Shades of Grey,' a trilogy of erotic, bondage-themed fiction. Dowd expressed surprise over the books' popularity, where a 21-year-old innocent girl becomes a sexual 'submissive' of a rich, powerful 27-year-old businessman. Frank Bruni's column, 'The Bleaker Sex,' reflects on Lena Dunham's new HBO series 'Girls,' noting its unglamorous and dull version of 'Sex in the City.' Both authors question whether today's sexual culture aligns with feminist ideals. The author suggests an alternative view on love and intimacy, citing George Eliot's 'Daniel Deronda.' The commentary concludes that deep sexual satisfaction is often found in traditional marriage.

article_content: England were terrific against Wales, but if I was at their team meeting at 'Pennyhill Park' on Monday morning, the first thing I would do is stick the 'RBS 6 Nations league table' on the whiteboard. England have turned an important corner, but they have achieved nothing yet. It's time to be hyper-critical and reset their goals. The players' celebrations were matched by head coach 'Stuart Lancaster's' and his backroom team. Against Italy, you go with the squad that did so well against Wales, although I would bring 'Courtney Lawes' back if fit. The great thing about Friday night in Cardiff was the hard-edged mental attitude and ruthless approach England displayed. England can achieve great things with that approach. Everybody expects them to beat Italy on Saturday, and this could easily be a week in which the intensity in training and playing drops off 10 per cent. I would challenge England to hit some easily measurable world-class standards against Italy. SET-PIECES MUST BE SLICKER. One hundred per cent scrum-possession from your put-in is a must. In the lineout, 95 per cent possession on your own throw is the standard required. England's lineout possession percentage must improve, while there were too many soft penalties given away. TOO MANY SOFT PENALTIES. England conceded nine in Cardiff, which is on the limit of what is acceptable. CUT DOWN ON CHARGEDOWNS. Three chargedowns is at least two too many. DON'T FORGET DROP GOALS. Whatever happened to the drop goal? I would ban all talk of any other nation and indeed the 'Six Nations Championship' generally, let alone the 'World Cup'. The focus should be totally on producing a world-class performance against Italy. IT'S AN 80 MINUTE GAME.

article_content: Reports of troop defections as 3-way ethnic alliance offensive presses into junta-held territory. By RFA Burmese 2023.11.15 -- Fierce fighting between Myanmar's military and ethnic armies in northern Shan state in recent weeks has expanded to include parts of the northwest, southeast and Rakhine state, displacing more than 500,000 people, according to 'unnamed sources'. Three weeks since the 'Three Brotherhood' Alliance of the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army, the Arakan Army and the Ta'ang National Liberation Army launched an offensive on Oct. 27 dubbed 'Operation 1027' the rebels have made 'significant gains' against the military in several key cities in Shan state in the country's northeast. In the wake of the operation, the Arakan Army, or AA, this week attacked the junta's military in the western state of Rakhine, ending a ceasefire brokered one year ago on 'questionable humanitarian grounds'. Conflict is also underway in Kayah state's Loikaw township, including 'unprecedented aerial bombardment' in urban areas causing 'excessive civilian casualties' But the fighting has taken a 'catastrophic humanitarian toll'. In a flash update published late on Tuesday, the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, or UNOCHA, said that more than 500,000 people had been displaced by fighting in the regions as of Nov. 14 - many of whom have moved towards the border with China to the north. The exodus included people who fled active war zones, as well as others who left their homes amid the threat of clashes, village raids by junta troops, and military artillery and air strikes, it said. 'A halt in clashes and provision of unimpeded humanitarian access by all parties are critical to safeguarding the lives and well-being of civilians and aid workers who are delivering life-saving services to people in need,' the UNOCHA said. The agency noted that key transportation routes in townships with active fighting have been blocked both by junta forces and ethnic armies, 'further restricting people's movements to safer locations as well as humanitarian access.' But UNOCHA said that, despite insecurity, access and telecommunications challenges in the regions, humanitarian assistance is continuing in northern Shan, while humanitarian partners in the northwest, southeast and Rakhine state are 'assessing new needs to respond accordingly.' 'Needs in the Northwest, Southeast and Rakhine are increasing by the day and require immediate response,' it said. More than 2 million civilians have fled their homes due to fighting since the military's Feb. 1, 2021 coup d'etat, according to 'unofficial figures' released by the UNOCHA at the end of last month. Artillery and air strikes The latest numbers suggest that the fears of those fleeing fighting in Myanmar are not unfounded. Sources in affected regions recently told RFA Burmese that more than 100 civilians were killed and at least 500 injured by junta artillery and air strikes in Myanmar over the last two months alone. The U.S.-based Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project, or ACLED, said it had documented at least 3,000 military artillery strikes and 2,000 air strikes in Myanmar between Feb. 1, 2021, and Nov. 10 this year, resulting in 2,000 and 2,500 fatalities, respectively. The number of military artillery and air strikes in Myanmar has steadily increased from 222 and 159 in the first quarter of this year to 500 and 400 in the third quarter, coinciding with reports of anti-junta forces winning an increasing number of battles on the ground. At least 30 civilians - including a pregnant woman and five children under the age of 10 - were killed by military air strikes from Nov. 12-14 in Sagaing region's Tigyaing township, residents of the township told RFA, amid a push by anti-junta forces to claim territory in the region. The strikes were carried out with 'advanced combat helicopters' on villages where people displaced by conflict have been sheltering, they said. Attempts by RFA to contact junta Deputy Information Minister Major Gen. Zaw Min Tun for comment on reports of civilian casualties resulting from military artillery and air strikes went unanswered Wednesday, but the junta has previously said that its forces do not target non-combatants. Poor morale and defections The military's shift in strategy to lean more heavily on artillery and air strikes also comes amid reports of poor morale in Myanmar's armed forces that sources say are a result of gains by the armed resistance and a realization that the military might not emerge the victor in its multi-front conflict. Sources say flagging morale has contributed to a number of military defections in recent months. On Tuesday, 50 junta soldiers stationed at Loikaw University in Kayah state - including Captain Kaung Myat, the commander of Light Infantry Battalion 6 - surrendered to local resistance forces together with their arms and ammunition after suffering a 'high number of casualties' in a clash with ethnic Karenni armed groups, the anti-junta Karen Nationalities Defense Force said in a statement. Days earlier, the entire Light Infantry Battalion 129, including its commander and 200 family members, surrendered to the Three Brotherhood Alliance's Myanmar National Democratic Alliance, or MNDAA, in northern Shan state. And on Oct. 30, all 60 members of Light Infantry Battalion 143, including a deputy commander and two company commanders, surrendered to the MNDAA in Shan's Kunlong township. Attempts by RFA to contact junta Social Affairs Minister Myint Kyi, who is also the spokesperson for the Kayah state government, for comment on the latest surrender went unanswered Wednesday. But the junta has signaled of late that it is concerned by gains by the resistance and their impact on support for his regime. Last week, junta chief Senior Gen. Min Aung Hlaing said that the alliance's 'Operation 1027' could 'break the country into pieces' if left unchecked. To boost the morale of troops and demonstrate public support for the military, the junta has organized several rallies in major cities in recent days, including Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyitaw, and Myitkyina. But residents of the cities told RFA on condition of anonymity that the rallies are part of a bid by the junta to 'hide its deteriorating political and military situation.'
